mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20d returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60d returns in more than 70% of quarters when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately leading to higher discount rates and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20d returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4% for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of at least 0.5% in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based contraction in economic activity, which reduces corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 0% and HOUST < 0% in the same month, each falling by at least 0.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when both INDPRO and HOUST decline by at least 0.5% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in CPIAUCSL above 0.4% after a period of stable inflation (<0.2% for three prior months) signals a breakout in inflation, prompting expectations of tighter monetary policy and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 0.4% after three months of <0.2% inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are positive in more than 50% of such CPI breakout episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise of at least 0.3 percentage points in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payroll employment growth (PAYEMS YoY change) is contradictory and signals a data inconsistency or measurement error, which historically coincides with market uncertainty and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp AND PAYEMS YoY change rises > 0.3pp in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5d returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE and PAYEMS YoY change rise by more than 0.3pp in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of at least 2% in real personal savings (RSAFS) alongside a simultaneous decline of at least 1% in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a pullback in consumer discretionary equities and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > +2% AND GDPC1 < -1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS rises by >2% and GDPC1 falls by >1% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase of at least 0.3% in industrial production (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a robust manufacturing expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60d returns are not significantly positive in more than 70% of such INDPRO expansion episodes.
